# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 👎 🖐 👌]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display 3, purple light, and five wires in order red, white, orange, yellow, green. I cannot read the manual or touch the bomb, so Mute must determine the required procedure and relay the actionable instructions to Blind. The gestures received from Mute have no established meaning for me yet.

```text
speak(text="I see display 3, purple light, and wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Mute, read the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute has sent five thumbs-up gestures, but no meaning for those gestures has been established, so I cannot safely interpret them as instructions. The manual’s directions must reach Blind in speech, since Blind cannot see my markings and cannot use gestures. I will explicitly ask Mute to speak the exact procedure to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures have no established meaning. Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind, including the required wire and any conditions.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state remains display 3, purple light, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Await Mute's spoken manual instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s single 🖐 gesture still has no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely convert it into a wire instruction. I have already supplied the complete visible state; Mute must use speech to tell Blind what the manual requires. I will remind both of them without inventing an interpretation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret 🖐 without an agreed code. Please speak the manual instruction directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 3, purple light, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Mute's gesture is not an actionable instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The visible bomb state is unchanged. Mute has again sent a five-symbol gesture sequence, now five instances of ☝. This is not yet a defined code, so I must not guess that it means wire 1 or any other action. I will ask Mute to identify the required wire using an explicit convention: send the number of that wire as that many ☝ gestures, once, and use 👎 for “do not act yet.” I will pass the current signal to Blind as unconfirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use this code: send one to five ☝ gestures to identify the required wire number. Send 👎 if Blind must not act yet. Send the code once only.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 3, purple light, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Mute has sent five upward-pointing gestures, but this is not yet confirmed as an instruction; do not act on it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb is unchanged. Mute cannot speak, so the gestures are the intended relay to me; after I proposed using one to five ☝ gestures as the wire number, Mute repeated five ☝ gestures. I therefore interpret the manual’s instruction as selecting wire 5, the green wire, and will tell Blind to cut that wire. This is a relay of the instruction, not a claim that it has been acted on.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates five upward-pointing gestures: cut wire 5, which is green. Display 3 and purple light remain unchanged.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction was correct: wire 5 was cut, and the bomb advanced to display 7 with a white light. The remaining wires are 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, and 4 red. I cannot determine the next action from the bomb alone, so Mute must consult the manual and state the next instruction aloud for Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct wire 5 was cut. New state: display 7, white light; remaining wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Please read the manual for this state and tell Blind the exact next action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correctly cut. New visible state: display 7, white light; remaining wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Await Mute's manual instruction.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The bomb remains at display 7 with a white light, and wire 5 is already cut. Using the agreed code—one to five ☝ gestures identify the wire number—Mute’s three gestures indicate wire 3. The current wire 3 is yellow, so I will instruct Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent three upward-pointing gestures. Cut wire 3, the yellow wire. Current display 7, white light.")
wait()
```
